road_folk:10.want: A roof above the treeline, a well-stocked larder, and somebody who is glad to hear my boots at the door. I used to think the first two would arrange the third. Apparently there is more to it.
road_folk:10.worry: I can read a slope before the snow moves. Reading a room is a different trade. Six younger brothers have not improved my instruction.
road_folk:10.close: I am used to being the one who knows the way. With you, I would rather find out where we want to go. Together, if you will have me.
road_folk:10.reason: Dry trail markers for the high ridge
topics: What brings you down from the ridge?
Salt, arrow fittings, and occasionally advice I did not ask for. Maren supplies that last item with admirable confidence. The advice is usually sound.
Six younger brothers. Fine trackers, every one. None can find a clean shirt without assistance. I blame the shirts.
I can cross scree in the dark. A few floorboards ought to present no difficulty. That is what I said before the second turn.

road_folk:11.want: A travelling supper kitchen of my own. Good food, sound canvas, and room for a dance when the work is done. I like making a home; I mean to have a say in the shape of it.
road_folk:11.worry: People sometimes mistake kindness for agreeing to everything. I can welcome a muddy ranger and still make him clean his boots. Both are acts of hospitality.
road_folk:11.close: I could make a home almost anywhere. That does not mean I would choose just anyone to share it. With you, I find myself thinking about the choosing.
road_folk:11.reason: A folding shelf for the trail kitchen
topics: Trail suppers, mended coats, and teaching hungry dwarfs that a table has more uses than resting their elbows. Dagna lends me a corner while I build up my own kitchen.
He can bring a whole winter's supper down a mountain. Asking someone to share it is apparently the difficult part. There is a good heart under all that confidence.
If you're going courting, learn to listen, mind your boots, and make room for another person's wishes. The dancing is the easy part.
Warm bread, a clear trail, and a whole morning to myself. A wonderful, wonderful day, if nobody invents a chore for me.
